keyFindings.description: The natsInCluster paragraph did not say that natsUrl must change in the same apply, nor that the hub must admit the pods' namespace first (clientNamespaces for gcp:ClusteredNatsHub); the natsReplicas paragraph did not name the hub's server count as the ceiling. Fixed as prose in dc1634a7868e.

An unset streamMaxBytes was described as each binary keeping 'its own default'; bus.ParseStreamMaxBytes sets no limit, so a deployed stream keeps the one it has. Fixed in dispatch.go (two comments), README.md and a dispatch_test.go comment and assertion message, in dc1634a7868e.

Three unchanged comments (dispatch_frontdoor.go file header, dispatch_kube.go dispatchSOCKS5Port and the front-door block) said every front-door pod runs the SOCKS5 proxy; with natsInCluster none does. Fixed in dc1634a7868e.

The comment claimed every Construct test 'carries them through the plugin' while none asserts the rendered values. Reworded in dc1634a7868e to what holds: the plugin decodes them (an undecodable value refuses the Construct), and their rendering is asserted on the direct path; the real-CLI proof's resolver refusal of natsReplicas 6 shows the plugin path decodes them.

Not a defect: the code-quality pass proposed one local-URL refusal for both modes, a socks5Server() helper beside socks5Proxy(), one table in place of the four natsInCluster tests, and a resolver function for the two numbers. The SOCKS5 mode's refusal text is kept byte for byte by design, the front door's bind address is a different value from the clients' proxy address, and TestDispatchAppAndListenerAgreeOnNats compares the two maps for equality (the count only pins that the mode renders every key), so none changes behaviour or hides an error.

Hardening, not a defect: with natsInCluster, NATS traffic is plaintext nats:// over the pod network, as the app-to-front-door SOCKS5 hop already was; the nkey challenge-response does not expose the seed.
